name: Closer
blurb: Real conversation that feels like winning.

cards.text: Tell them the specific thing they did this week that you keep replaying in your head. Specific or it doesn't count.
Finish this out loud, one each: 'I've been wanting to tell you…' No interruptions — the blank does the work.
cards.soften: Write it down, trade papers, read theirs silently.

cards.text: One true thing each, 60 seconds. The listener's only job is to listen — no fixing, no comebacks. Then trade.
If our relationship were a song right now, what's playing? Name it and defend it in one sentence.
What's something you miss that we used to do — not from lack of trying, just life? Name it. It goes back on the calendar this week.
Hold their hands and look at their eyes. Say the thing you've been carrying this week that's heavier than it should be.
cards.speak: They just hold your hands. That's the whole rule.
cards.soften: Sit back-to-back and say it without eye contact.

cards.text: The menu game: each build a three-item menu — one thing you want more of, one you want less of, one you're curious to try. Trade menus. Each picks one item to 'order' this week.
Make one wish about us out loud. The other answers either 'wish granted' (this week) or 'wish deferred' (name a date). No negotiating, no explaining.
Plan our next perfect Sunday out loud, minute by minute, starting at 9am. Both hands on the wheel.
Do one tiny act of service for them right now, without asking what they want. They close their eyes while you decide.
cards.soften: Tell them what you WOULD do, and when.

cards.text: What's a question you wish I'd ask you more often? I'm asking it now. Answer it slow.
Each say one thing you'd change about us if you had a magic wand. Wand-holders collect wishes — no defending, no explaining, just 'ok'. Wishes get re-read next month.
cards.soften: One wish each, deferred answers allowed.

cards.text: Slowly take off one item of their choosing.
cards.speak: While you do, tell them what you love about the person underneath, not just the skin.
cards.soften: Hold their hand against your heart for 30 seconds instead.

cards.text: Whisper the moment you knew you were done for. Be precise — the minute, the light, the sound in the room.
Kiss their neck for 30 slow seconds.
cards.speak: While you do, tell them the moment this week you were proudest of them.

cards.text: Trade answers: what's a small thing the other did today that you noticed and appreciated silently? Silent appreciations get said now.
Tell them one thing they did this week that you keep replaying in your head.
What is a small everyday moment with them that still feels like a win when you think about it?
Share one way they made ordinary time feel better recently without even trying.
What is something you want more of from them that would make the weeks feel lighter?
Tell them about a quiet hope you have for the two of you over the next month.
What is one wish you have about us that you've been carrying but haven't said out loud yet?
Describe a recent moment when you felt especially glad to be on the same team.
Invite them to hear one specific appreciation you've been holding onto, then stay quiet while they take it in.
cards.speak: I've been meaning to tell you this because it stuck with me.
cards.soften: Share one short thing you appreciated about them this week.

cards.text: Offer a listen-first minute: ask them what would feel good to talk about right now, then only listen and reflect back what you heard.
cards.soften: Ask what is on their mind and give them space to answer fully.

cards.text: Make one clear wish about the two of you and invite them to answer with either 'wish granted this week' or 'wish deferred' plus a date.
cards.soften: Share one small hopeful wish and ask how it lands.

cards.text: Invite a soft trade: say 'I want more of ___ from you, and in exchange I'll give you ___' and mean both parts.
cards.speak: This is what would feel really good to receive, and here's what I want to offer back.
cards.soften: Share one thing you'd like more of and one thing you're happy to give.

cards.text: Offer to replay a specific kind moment from this week out loud, adding why it still matters to you.
cards.soften: Mention one kind thing they did and why it landed well.

cards.text: Together, each build a three-item want-menu of small things that would make the coming week better. Trade menus and circle one item you can actually give.
cards.soften: Each name one small thing that would help, then choose one to try.

cards.text: Take turns granting or deferring one wish each. The grantor says 'wish granted this week' or 'wish deferred' and names a realistic date.
cards.soften: Each share one small wish and respond with a kind yes or later.

cards.text: Do a listen-first round: each person gets ninety seconds to speak about anything on their mind while the other only listens, then reflects one sentence back.
cards.soften: Each share for thirty seconds while the other simply listens.

cards.text: Trade framing challenge: each completes the sentence 'I want more of ___ from you, and in exchange I'll give you ___'. Both parts must feel genuine.
cards.soften: Each name one want and one offering in a lighter way.

cards.text: Together, name three specific things the other person did this month that still feel good to remember. Keep going until you both have a short list.
cards.soften: Each share one recent thing the other did that landed well.

cards.text: What is one small thing that always makes you feel a little more settled when you're around them?
Share a tiny detail from today that you are glad you got to experience with them, even if it was ordinary.
What is a simple way they could surprise you this week that would feel thoughtful rather than big?
Name one everyday ritual between you that you would miss if it disappeared.
Talk about the difference between a week that feels connected and a week that feels like you are just sharing a calendar.
Share what 'feeling chosen' looks like in ordinary days, not just special ones.
Discuss one small trade that would make both of you feel more supported in the next couple of weeks.
